arguments.content: Pursuant to Rule 12(b)(6), Defendant respectfully requests dismissal of the complaint for failure to state a claim upon which relief may be granted. Legal standards are well-established: a complaint must contain sufficient factual matter, accepted as true, to 'state a claim to relief that is plausible on its face.' Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662, 678 (2009). Plaintiff's allegations consist of conclusory statements devoid of factual enhancement, amounting to little more than a 'formulaic recitation of the elements.' Bell Atl. Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 555 (2007). Such pleading fails to cross 'the line between possibility and plausibility.' Id. at 570. Defendant has no knowledge of the allegations in Paragraphs 12–18, and they appear factually unsupported. No duty of care is established under applicable state law. The motion is filed in good faith and with proper authority. Respectfully submitted, [Attorney Name], Esq.
